A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AQCP study. Their complete main texts, equations, Algorithm 1, Figures 1–5, and Appendices A–C are readable and support comparison despite pagination changes.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original multimodal-regression experiments using ibm_sherbrooke hardware and classical simulators, including coverage and prediction-set efficiency results.

after.justification: Section 5 retains the original hardware and simulation experiments and their coverage and efficiency results in Figures 2–5.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 makes appending test scores to calibration optional, whereas v1's pseudocode always appends them, explicitly accommodating Theorem 2's fixed-calibration case. Section 4.2 also revises KDE normalization from h to h^d and makes HDR density level sets inclusive. The core feedback rule, model, and evaluated updating variant remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic univariate multimodal-regression distribution, ibm_sherbrooke hardware, and simulator scenarios. Corrected hardware labels in the coverage captions agree with v1's experimental text and do not establish changed coverage.

E2.justification: The coverage comparator remains AQCP's zero-step-size counterpart with expanding calibration; v2 names it online QCP. Figure 5 retains the same score-function comparisons and optimal prediction-set reference.

E3.justification: The reported experimental settings remain unchanged, including the five-qubit, five-layer model, 100 initial calibration points, 9,900 test points, 500-point coverage window, 90% target coverage, and shot-number sweep. The expanded evaluation description explains the existing protocol.

E4.justification: The adaptivity, score-function, and shot-number analyses in Figures 3–5 are retained. Section 5.4 proposes controlled noise perturbations, multiday evaluation, and step-size sensitivity analysis as future work; it does not report these additional tests.

E5.justification: Both versions report coverage curves and aggregate averages without repeated-run or seed counts, empirical confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: The local-coverage and efficiency curves in Figures 3–5 match, and the associated findings remain unchanged. Figure 2 retains the same shot-distribution comparison with different rendering. No empirical result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: Appendices B–C substantially revise optimality theory. Theorems 3–4 change from necessary-and-sufficient characterizations to sufficient conditions, with new no-flat-spots assumptions, almost-everywhere qualifications, and a definition requiring optimality across all coverage levels. Their proofs are rewritten, replacing boundary-randomization arguments and correcting threshold directions. The Gaussian examples are restricted appropriately, while Theorem 2 clarifies its fixed-calibration and Markov assumptions and gains an explicit spectral-gap definition.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the central claims: hardware drift threatens score exchangeability, AQCP supplies asymptotic average coverage under arbitrary hardware noise, and the experiments show improved coverage stability. The appendix's narrower optimality results do not redefine these principal contributions.

C2.justification: New Section 5.4 explicitly identifies batch prediction as unsupported and explains the need for stronger drift and sensitivity evaluation. New Appendix B.4 distinguishes oracle optimality from practical AQCP guarantees involving estimation, finite shots, and calibration. Section 5.2 also softens causal noise attribution; the single-day and attribution caveats already appeared in v1's conclusion.

D1.justification: Section 5 replaces code and data availability upon request with a GitHub repository pointer. Section 5.1.2 explicitly confirms that experiments include calibration updates. These improve access and implementation documentation without establishing rerun experiments.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion adds Tasar's quantum-entanglement work and acknowledges broader quantum conformal research while retaining the non-stationary-noise gap. Other additions include Schuld, Jiang, Podkopaev, and Born references; Gustafson–Sigal and Rényi are removed. The main positioning relative to QCP and ACI remains intact.

P1.justification: The revision corrects grammar, terminology, affiliations, and notation, and tightens background and experimental explanations. Exchangeability becomes Section 2.1.1, the implementation subsection is retitled, and limitations and the optimality-to-AQCP connection receive dedicated subsections. The overall narrative organization remains recognizable.

P2.justification: Figures 3–4 lose contradictory FakeQuitoV2 caption text, and Figure 4 replaces repetitive subcaptions with short labels and a shared caption. Figure 2 is rasterized, Algorithm 1 moves, and journal headers alter page layout. All five figures remain.

improvement.justification: The revision improves precision by replacing overbroad optimality characterizations with assumption-qualified sufficient results and correcting proof thresholds in Appendices B–C. Clearer applicability limits, corrected captions, and a code/data repository pointer improve interpretation and reproducibility documentation. These benefits strengthen the supporting material while the central AQCP contribution and empirical evidence remain essentially unchanged.
